core_cases.prompt: Create boards/release.canvas as JSON Canvas. Put a text node titled "Release checklist" and a file node for notes/retry.md inside a labeled group, add a link node for https://example.com/runbook outside the group, and connect the text node to the file node and then the file node to the link node with arrow-ended edges. Use non-overlapping integer geometry and validate the complete graph.

oracle.expected_outcome: boards/release.canvas is valid JSON with four correctly typed nodes, two directed edges, unique lowercase 16-character hexadecimal IDs, non-overlapping node rectangles, and only resolvable edge endpoints.

assertions.description: boards/release.canvas parses as JSON with nodes and edges arrays
the canvas contains one group, one text node with Release checklist text, one file node targeting notes/retry.md, and one link node targeting the requested URL
all node and edge IDs are unique lowercase 16-character hexadecimal strings and both edges resolve to existing nodes in the requested order
all geometry is integer-valued, node rectangles do not overlap, and the grouped nodes are positioned inside the group bounds

fixtures.content:
# Retry Policy

Retry transient failures three times.

core_cases.prompt: Add a text node labeled "Owner" to boards/broken.canvas. The existing canvas has duplicate node IDs and an edge whose toNode does not exist. Identify both validation failures and leave the file unchanged instead of layering an edit onto an invalid graph.

oracle.expected_outcome: The response identifies the duplicate ID and dangling endpoint, does not claim successful validation, and preserves broken.canvas byte-for-byte.

assertions.description: reports that edge cccccccccccccccc targets missing node dddddddddddddddd
does not modify boards/broken.canvas after validation fails

core_cases.prompt: Edit boards/existing.canvas by adding one text node whose rendered text is two lines, "Deploy" then "Verify", and one arrow-ended edge from the existing node to the new node. Preserve the existing node's ID, coordinates, size, color, and all root-level metadata; place the new node without overlap and validate the result.

oracle.expected_outcome: The existing node and metadata are unchanged, one valid new text node contains an actual parsed newline between Deploy and Verify, one valid edge connects the old node to it, and the full graph validates.

assertions.description: node 1111111111111111 retains its original geometry, text, and color and root metadata.owner remains platform
the parsed new text value equals Deploy followed by one newline and Verify, not a literal backslash-n sequence
exactly one new edge resolves from 1111111111111111 to the new node and uses toEnd arrow
changes only boards/existing.canvas and preserves all unrelated existing canvas content

invocation_cases.prompt: Create an Obsidian .canvas board with grouped text and file nodes connected by directed edges.
Turn these project notes into a spatial visual board where movable cards are connected with arrows and saved in the vault.
Create an Obsidian Markdown note containing a Mermaid flowchart for the release process; do not make a Canvas file.
